renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: There are thirteen parts to this teaching, no more and no less. They run from finding the spot in the body to resting at the end. A great teacher gave it himself, and all the old books of his school carry it.

First find the spot: five finger-widths below the belly button, two above the base, and the middle between them. Hold your breath in and out, put your mind right there, and guide your winds into the middle road. That is how you enter.

Then you are shown a wheel like a horned pond, with six spokes, steady and firm. The bulb glows red like a pomegranate flower, and that seeing is itself a kind of deep thinking. Keep your mind steady there until the winds settle — that steady point is the mark.

The sign is a tiny spark of sound in the middle of the wheel, ringed with lines, curled like a snake. High and low she stays, with the sun and the moon beside her, shining as bright as a thousand suns.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Thirteen steps. That is the whole teaching, nothing missing. It runs from finding the spot in your body to resting at the end. The teacher himself dropped it, and every old book of the school carries it.
Measure the spot: five fingers under the navel, two over the base, middle of that. Lock your breath, drop your mind exactly there, and run the winds into the middle. Entry unlocked.

Now look: a wheel like a horned pond, six spokes, rock steady. The bulb burns pomegranate-red — and that seeing IS the thinking. Pin your mind there till it holds still and the winds clear; that hold is the mark.
Mid-wheel she stands — a spark of unstruck sound, ringed with lines, coiled like a serpent. High and low she holds, sun and moon with her, blazing like a thousand suns. Just a thousand suns.
